column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|01-01|379|Μέγας Βασίλειος|Basil the Great|Basil was born in Caesarea in Cappadocia and studied in Athens, where he met Gregory of Nazianzus. He became bishop of Caesarea and was a great theologian and organiser. He founded charitable institutions and wrote ascetic and doctrinal works. The Church honours him as one of the Three Hierarchs.

bio|01-07|1934|Τάσος Παπαδόπουλος|Tassos Papadopoulos|Tassos Papadopoulos was born in Nicosia and studied law. As a young man he took part in the EOKA struggle and later became a member of parliament and a minister. In 2003 he was elected President of the Republic of Cyprus, and during his term Cyprus joined the European Union. He died in 2008.

bio|01-13|2012|Ραούφ Ντενκτάς|Rauf Denktaş|Rauf Denktaş was a Turkish Cypriot politician and lawyer. He led the Turkish Cypriot community for decades and in 1983 declared the "Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus", which was not recognised internationally. He was the main interlocutor in the negotiations on the Cyprus problem until 2005.

bio|01-20|1906|Αριστοτέλης Ωνάσης|Aristotle Onassis|Aristotle Onassis was born in Smyrna and after the Catastrophe left for Argentina, where he began trading. He became one of the richest shipowners in the world and founded Olympic Airways. He married Jackie Kennedy and left his fortune to a foundation that bears his name.

bio|01-25|390|Γρηγόριος Ναζιανζηνός|Gregory of Nazianzus|Gregory was born near Nazianzus in Cappadocia and studied in Athens. He became a bishop and for a short time Patriarch of Constantinople. His theological orations on the Holy Trinity earned him the title "the Theologian". The Church honours him as one of the Three Hierarchs.

bio|02-12|1933|Κώστας Γαβράς|Costa-Gavras|Costa-Gavras was born in Arcadia and became a film director in France. He became famous for political films such as "Z" and "Missing". For "Z" he won the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film, and he was head of the French Cinémathèque.

bio|02-26|1938|Ευαγόρας Παλληκαρίδης|Evagoras Pallikarides|Evagoras Pallikarides was born in the district of Paphos and was a pupil at the Paphos gymnasium. He joined EOKA as a teenager and was arrested by the British. He was sentenced to death and hanged in 1957, at the age of nineteen, and is regarded as a national hero.

bio|02-29|1940|Βαρθολομαίος|Bartholomew|Bartholomew was born on Imbros and became a cleric and theologian. In 1991 he was elected Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople. He is known for his support of inter-Christian dialogue and for his work to protect the environment, which is why he is called the "Green Patriarch".

bio|03-01|1896|Δημήτρης Μητρόπουλος|Dimitri Mitropoulos|Dimitri Mitropoulos was born in Athens and studied music in Europe. He became a great conductor and pianist and conducted major orchestras in the United States, such as the New York Philharmonic. He also composed, and he was known for memorising entire scores.

bio|03-04|1968|Κυριάκος Μητσοτάκης|Kyriakos Mitsotakis|Kyriakos Mitsotakis was born in Athens and studied at Harvard and Stanford. He worked in finance and in 2004 was elected a member of parliament. In 2016 he became leader of New Democracy and since 2019 he has been prime minister of Greece.

bio|03-08|415|Υπατία|Hypatia|Hypatia was a philosopher, mathematician and astronomer in Alexandria, the daughter of the mathematician Theon. She taught philosophy and was respected in the city. She was murdered by a Christian mob in 415 amid the political conflicts of the time and became a symbol of science and freedom of speech.

bio|03-08|1907|Κωνσταντίνος Καραμανλής|Konstantinos Karamanlis|Konstantinos Karamanlis was born in Proti, Serres, and became a lawyer and politician. He was prime minister in the 1950s and 1960s and, after the dictatorship, again in 1974, when he restored democracy. He led Greece into the EEC and served twice as President of the Republic.

bio|03-13|1900|Γιώργος Σεφέρης|George Seferis|George Seferis was born in Smyrna and studied law in Paris. He worked as a diplomat and wrote poetry that combines tradition with modern experience, in works such as "Turning Point" and "Logbook". In 1963 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-15|1975|Αριστοτέλης Ωνάσης|Aristotle Onassis|Aristotle Onassis died in Paris in 1975 after a serious illness. He had been born in Smyrna and had become one of the greatest shipowners in the world. His fortune passed to his daughter Christina and to a foundation in memory of his son Alexander.

bio|03-18|1996|Οδυσσέας Ελύτης|Odysseas Elytis|Odysseas Elytis died in Athens in 1996. He was a poet of the Generation of the '30s and wrote works such as "Axion Esti", which Mikis Theodorakis set to music. For the whole of his work he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1979.

bio|03-29|1943|Βαγγέλης (Ευάγγελος Παπαθανασίου)|Vangelis (Evangelos Papathanassiou)|Vangelis Papathanassiou was born in Volos and grew up in Athens. He became known as a composer of electronic music and was first a member of Aphrodite's Child. He wrote the music for "Chariots of Fire" and for films such as "Blade Runner", and won an Oscar.

bio|04-07|1614|Δομήνικος Θεοτοκόπουλος|Domenikos Theotokopoulos|Domenikos Theotokopoulos, known as El Greco, was born in Candia (Heraklion) on Crete. He trained in Byzantine painting and continued his studies in Venice and Rome. From 1577 he lived in Toledo, Spain, where he created his works in a characteristic elongated style.

bio|04-08|1798|Διονύσιος Σολωμός|Dionysios Solomos|Dionysios Solomos was born on Zakynthos and studied in Italy. He chose to write in the demotic language and was called the national poet. He wrote the "Hymn to Liberty", of which the first two stanzas became the national anthem of Greece and Cyprus.

bio|04-24|1919|Γλαύκος Κληρίδης|Glafcos Clerides|Glafcos Clerides was born in Nicosia and studied law in London. He fought as a pilot in the Second World War and was a lawyer and politician. He was president of the House of Representatives and later President of the Republic of Cyprus from 1993 to 2003.

bio|04-29|1863|Κωνσταντίνος Καβάφης|Constantine Cavafy|Constantine Cavafy was born in Alexandria and lived there most of his life. He worked as a clerk and published his poems in small pamphlets. He wrote poems on historical and erotic themes, such as "Ithaka" and "Waiting for the Barbarians", and is one of the greatest poets of modern Greek literature.

bio|05-02|373|Αθανάσιος|Athanasius|Athanasius was bishop of Alexandria and a great defender of Orthodox teaching against Arianism. He took part in the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea. He was exiled many times for his positions and wrote important theological works. The Church honours him as Athanasius the Great.

bio|05-11|482|Ιουστινιανός Α´|Justinian I|Justinian was born in a village of Macedonia or Illyria and became emperor in 527. He tried to recover the western provinces of the empire, and his victories were won by generals such as Belisarius. He codified Roman law and built Hagia Sophia.

bio|05-29|1922|Ιάννης Ξενάκης|Iannis Xenakis|Iannis Xenakis was born in Brăila, Romania, to Greek parents. He left as a political refugee for France, where he worked as an architect with Le Corbusier. He became a composer and used mathematics, statistics and computers in his music.

bio|06-11|1922|Μιχάλης Κακογιάννης|Michael Cacoyannis|Michael Cacoyannis was born in Limassol and studied in London. He became a film director and brought "Electra" and "Zorba the Greek" to the screen. He was a pioneer of Greek cinema, and his films became known abroad too.

bio|06-15|1946|Ντέμης Ρούσσος|Demis Roussos|Demis Roussos was born in Alexandria, Egypt. He was a member of Aphrodite's Child with Vangelis Papathanassiou and then began an international career as a soloist. His distinctive voice made songs such as "Forever and Ever" known in many countries.

bio|06-17|1985|Μάρκος Παγδατής|Marcos Baghdatis|Marcos Baghdatis was born in Limassol and became a professional tennis player. He reached finals of international tournaments and rose into the top ten of the world rankings. In 2006 he reached the final of the Australian Open, and he is the best-known tennis player from Cyprus.

bio|06-23|1897|Γεώργιος Γρίβας|Georgios Grivas|Georgios Grivas was born in Cyprus and served in the Greek army, where he reached the rank of colonel. He organised and led EOKA in the 1955-1959 struggle against British rule. Later he returned to Cyprus to oppose the policies of Makarios.

bio|07-07|1936|Νίκος Ξυλούρης|Nikos Xylouris|Nikos Xylouris was born in Anogeia on Crete and became one of the most important singers in the country. He sang Cretan music and the songs of the generation of Theodorakis and Hadjidakis. He was known as the "Archangel of Crete", and his songs became symbols of resistance.

bio|07-21|1425|Μανουήλ Β΄ Παλαιολόγος|Manuel II Palaiologos|Manuel II Palaiologos was Byzantine emperor from 1391. He travelled to Western Europe to ask for help against the Ottomans and lived through the siege of Constantinople by Bayezid. He was also a scholar and wrote theological and rhetorical works.

bio|07-23|1957|Νίκος Γκάλης|Nikos Galis|Nikos Galis was born in New Jersey in the United States and grew up in Greece. He played for Aris Thessaloniki and became the greatest Greek basketball player of his time. He was the leading figure of the national team that won EuroBasket 1987.

bio|07-26|811|Νικηφόρος Α´|Nikephoros I|Nikephoros I was Byzantine emperor from 802, when he deposed the empress Irene. He made administrative and tax reforms and fought the Bulgarians. He was killed in 811 in battle with Krum, in the area of the Balkans.

bio|07-29|1925|Μίκης Θεοδωράκης|Mikis Theodorakis|Mikis Theodorakis was born on Chios and grew up in various cities. He composed symphonic works, set poetry to music and wrote the music of "Zorba the Greek". He was a political activist and was imprisoned under the junta, and to this day his songs remain the voice of the people.

bio|08-13|1913|Μακάριος Γ΄|Makarios III|Makarios III was born in the village of Panayia in Paphos and became Archbishop of Cyprus in 1950. He led the struggle for independence and in 1960 became the first President of the Republic of Cyprus. He remained in power until his death in 1977.

bio|08-29|1931|Στέλιος Καζαντζίδης|Stelios Kazantzidis|Stelios Kazantzidis was born in Nea Kosmos, Athens. He became the best-loved popular singer of the 1950s and 1960s and sang about the lives of migrants and the poor. With his voice, songs such as "Ena to helidoni" became classics.

bio|09-07|1909|Ελία Καζάν|Elia Kazan|Elia Kazan was born in Constantinople to Greek parents and grew up in the United States. He became a director in the theatre and in film, a founder of the Actors Studio, and directed films such as "A Streetcar Named Desire" and "On the Waterfront". He won two Oscars for directing.

bio|09-13|1873|Κωνσταντίνος Καραθεοδωρή|Constantin Carathéodory|Constantin Carathéodory was born in Berlin to a Constantinopolitan Greek family. He was a mathematician and taught at German universities. He worked on measure theory, the calculus of variations and thermodynamics, and took part in founding the University of Smyrna.

bio|09-15|668|Κώνστας Β΄|Constans II|Constans II was Byzantine emperor from 641. He fought the Arabs, who defeated him at the Battle of the Masts, and spent his last years in Sicily. He was assassinated in 668 in Syracuse.

bio|09-16|1977|Μαρία Κάλλας|Maria Callas|Maria Callas died in Paris in 1977, at the age of fifty-three. Born in New York to Greek parents, she had become the most famous soprano of the 20th century, known as "La Divina". Her death brought great sadness to the world of opera.

bio|09-20|1971|Γιώργος Σεφέρης|George Seferis|George Seferis died in Athens in 1971, during the dictatorship of the colonels. In 1969 he had published a statement condemning the regime. His funeral became the occasion for a large popular demonstration against the regime.

bio|09-24|1180|Μανουήλ Α΄ Κομνηνός|Manuel I Komnenos|Manuel I Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1143. He developed relations with the West and fought in Italy and in the Balkans. He was defeated by the Seljuks at Myriokephalon in 1176 and died in 1180.

bio|09-27|1946|Νίκος Αναστασιάδης|Nicos Anastasiades|Nicos Anastasiades was born in Limassol and studied law in London. He was leader of the Democratic Rally party and in 2013 was elected President of the Republic of Cyprus. He was re-elected in 2018 and remained in office until 2023.

bio|10-01|1541|Δομήνικος Θεοτοκόπουλος|Domenikos Theotokopoulos|Domenikos Theotokopoulos was born in 1541 in Candia on Crete, which was then a Venetian possession. He became an icon painter of the Cretan school and later travelled to Italy. He became known as El Greco and is the most important Greek painter of the Renaissance.

bio|10-05|578|Ιουστίνος Β΄|Justin II|Justin II was Byzantine emperor from 565 and the successor of Justinian. During his reign the Lombards invaded Italy and he fought the Persians. In his last years he was ill and Tiberius took over his duties.

bio|10-13|1934|Νάνα Μούσχουρη|Nana Mouskouri|Nana Mouskouri was born in Chania on Crete and studied music in Athens. She began with Manos Hadjidakis and later developed an international career. She sang in many languages and sold millions of records.

bio|10-13|1971|Πύρρος Δήμας|Pyrros Dimas|Pyrros Dimas was born in Albania to a Greek minority family and moved to Greece. He became a weightlifter and won gold medals at the Olympic Games of 1992, 1996 and 2000. He is one of the greatest Greek athletes.

bio|10-23|1925|Μάνος Χατζιδάκις|Manos Hadjidakis|Manos Hadjidakis was born in Xanthi and lived in Athens. He composed the music for films such as "Never on Sunday", for which he won an Oscar, and wrote songs that are important in modern Greek music. He founded and directed the Third Programme of ERT.

bio|10-26|1957|Νίκος Καζαντζάκης|Nikos Kazantzakis|Nikos Kazantzakis died in Germany in 1957 while on a journey. Born in Heraklion, he wrote novels such as "Zorba the Greek" and "Christ Recrucified", and the "Odyssey". His grave is in Heraklion.

bio|10-28|1932|Σπύρος Κυπριανού|Spyros Kyprianou|Spyros Kyprianou was born in Limassol and studied law in London. He was foreign minister under Makarios and founded the DIKO party. After the death of Makarios in 1977 he became President of the Republic of Cyprus until 1988.

bio|11-02|1911|Οδυσσέας Ελύτης|Odysseas Elytis|Odysseas Elytis was born in Heraklion on Crete and lived in Athens. His real name was Odysseas Alepoudelis. He was a poet of the Generation of the '30s with a strong reference to the Aegean and the sun, and in 1979 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|11-11|1028|Κωνσταντίνος Η΄|Constantine VIII|Constantine VIII was a Byzantine emperor and the brother of Basil II. He was co-emperor from 976 and became sole emperor in 1025. His reign lasted three years and is considered incompetent. He died in 1028.

bio|11-14|565|Ιουστινιανός Α´|Justinian I|Justinian I died in 565 in Constantinople, after a reign of thirty-eight years. He left behind the Code of Justinian and Hagia Sophia, while his wars had exhausted the state. He was succeeded by his nephew Justin II.

bio|12-02|1923|Μαρία Κάλλας|Maria Callas|Maria Callas was born in New York to Greek parents and studied music in Athens. She became an international soprano and sang at La Scala in Milan and at the Metropolitan Opera. Her performances in "Norma" and "Tosca" are considered among the greatest in the history of opera.

bio|12-06|1994|Γιάννης Αντετοκούνμπο|Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis Antetokounmpo was born in Athens to parents who had come from Nigeria and started out with Filathlitikos. He played in the NBA for the Milwaukee Bucks and became a two-time MVP. In 2021 he won the championship with his team.

bio|12-11|711|Ιουστινιανός Β´|Justinian II|Justinian II was a Byzantine emperor twice. He became emperor in 685, was deposed and had his nose cut off, and returned to the throne in 705 with the help of the Bulgarians. He was assassinated in 711 and was succeeded by Philippikos.

bio|12-11|969|Νικηφόρος Β´ Φωκάς|Nikephoros II Phokas|Nikephoros II Phokas was a Byzantine general and emperor from 963. He recovered Crete and Cyprus from the Arabs and conquered Cilicia. He was assassinated in 969 in a conspiracy led by John Tzimiskes.

bio|12-11|1282|Μιχαήλ Η´ Παλαιολόγος|Michael VIII Palaiologos|Michael VIII Palaiologos was emperor of Nicaea and became the founder of the Palaiologan dynasty. In 1261 he recaptured Constantinople from the Latins. He sought the union of the Churches, which brought him into conflict with many of his subjects.
